messages:
incident-bot: Paging @oncall (primary): severity=sev2 — elevated KMS API latency/errors observed causing signing failures for service startups and request auth. Alerting from: auth-service, signer-proxy. @Alice Nguyen tagged as recent owner.

Alice Nguyen: just hit this in prod — lots of auth-service pods failing startup with `Error: signing failed: KMS::Timeout` and crashloops. Rolling deploys also seeing >50% provisioning errors.

Priya Shah: seeing the same across us-west-2. Logs show repeated 504/429 from AWS KMS when trying to GenerateDataKey/Sign. Example: ```
2026-03-15T16:02:33Z auth-service ERROR signing failed: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = KMS request timeout status=504
2026-03-15T16:02:34Z signer-proxy WARN AWS KMS Rate exceeded: RequestThrottled
```

Jamal Ortiz: customers impacted: dedicated tenants with keys in us-west-2 and some hosted-auth flows. Metric spikes: signer error rate from 0.3% -> 18% starting ~16:01 UTC. Sending initial incident severity=sev2.

Marta Lopez: quick mitigation ideas: 1) enable in-process soft signer fallback (software-based signing) for new starts 2) increase KMS retry/backoff and reduce parallel signing concurrency 3) switch a small subset to a different region key (eu-west-1) for validation. Which are feasible now?

Alice Nguyen: we have a feature flag `REDWOOD_KMS_SOFT_SIGNER` that allows ephemeral software signing for non-PII requests — can flip for affected pools. Also we have a cached key material layer (KV cache) but TTL currently 5m — can bump to 24h.

Priya Shah: I'm going to open a support case with AWS KMS and get their status. For now, let's reduce pod churn: pause any automatic restarts/rollouts touching auth-service and signer-proxy. @Ops Pager can you stop the deploys? :pray:

Ops Pager: paused CI->prod deploy pipeline for auth-service and signer-proxy. Notified release-team.

Jamal Ortiz: AWS status: I checked https://status.aws.amazon.com — no global outage listed. Opening case: case# 1234567890 (internal ref). Reached TAM, they are investigating throttling in us-west-2 for KMS endpoints.

Alice Nguyen: rolling mitigation plan: (A) flip soft signer for pod startup so new pods don't call KMS at boot (B) increase local key cache TTL (C) reduce signing concurrency from 50 -> 10 per instance (D) implement transient 30s exponential backoff with jitter. I'll apply A+B now to one canary node pool.

Priya Shah: suggest we also reduce request retries from clients to avoid amplifying KMS load. Update gateway config `signer.retry.max_attempts` = 3, `backoff.base_ms` = 200.

Marta Lopez: patch snippet for feature flag set in k8s: ```yaml
- name: REDWOOD_KMS_SOFT_SIGNER
  value: "true"
- name: REDWOOD_KMS_KEY_CACHE_TTL_SEC
  value: "86400" # 24h
```
I'll apply to canary namespace.

Alice Nguyen: applied flag to canary for signer-proxy-canary (replicas=2). Restarted pods. Monitoring logs.

(infra-rotations-bot): deploy-bot: rollout started for signer-proxy-canary by Alice Nguyen at 16:10 UTC.

Priya Shah: AWS support responded — they see elevated throttling for customer KMS requests in us-west-2, advising to reduce high-frequency GenerateDataKey/Sign calls and use local caching where possible. They also gave a temporary region fallback recommendation.

Jamal Ortiz: can confirm error rate in canary dropped from 60% -> 8% after soft signer + cache TTL bump. Starting to roll to 10% of capacity.

Alice Nguyen: customer impact assessment: user-facing errors primarily are 502/500 during startup and auth handshake failures for APIs that require signing. Estimated affected traffic: peak 12% of requests for us-west-2 served customers, mostly dedicated customers with pinned keys in us-west-2. No data exfiltration. No key compromise.

Marta Lopez: communicate to support: prepare an external blameless note: "We are experiencing elevated request signing errors due to increased KMS API latency in AWS us-west-2. We have applied mitigations including software fallback signing and extended local key caching; we are working with AWS support. Some customers may see transient auth errors and delayed pod startups."

Priya Shah: AWS case# 1234567890 escalated to KMS engineering. They suggested two medium-term options: (1) replicate keys to an alternate region and use regional routing (2) provision a dedicated KMS throughput increase (account-level request quota bump) via TAM.

Jamal Ortiz: action items: 
- Alice: continue roll soft-signer + cache rollout to 30% by 16:25 UTC, then 100% if stable.
- Priya: keep AWS case open and push for quota/mitigation.
- Marta: draft customer comms and coordinate with support.
- Ops Pager: ensure deploys remain paused until safe.

Alice Nguyen: taking ownership for the next 4 hours. Handoff: @Priya will be primary AWS communication. If anything degrades, page me directly.

Ops Pager: CI pause remains in effect. If you need Canary -> Prod fast-track, use `emergency-release` with approvals from Alice + Marta.

Priya Shah: update 16:22 UTC — AWS says they applied configuration changes to reduce internal throttling; monitoring shows slow improvement. Keep mitigations in place for at least 1 hour.

Jamal Ortiz: metrics note: signer error rate now 3.5%, latency for sign operations returning towards baseline but still intermittently spiking. No additional customer pages in last 10m.

Marta Lopez: posted draft incident notice to #customer-status-drafts for review.

Alice Nguyen: starting gradual rollout to 50% now. Observability: trace of a previously failing startup now succeeds with soft signer and cached key.

incident-bot: Incident updated to status=mitigated (partial). Details: mitigations applied, vendor engagement ongoing.

Priya Shah: will keep the case open and update when AWS confirms steady-state. Planning postmortem after resolution — focus on reducing synchronous KMS calls during startup and adding regional failover in the signer library.

Marta Lopez: I will schedule a 1-hour post-incident sync tomorrow and own customer communication.

Alice Nguyen: leaving a note for on-call rotation: if this returns, immediate steps: 1) pause deploys 2) flip soft-sign 3) expand cache TTL 4) fallback region routing.

infra-rotations-bot: oncall handoff at 16:30 UTC — primary oncall now Priya Shah for next shift.

Priya Shah: handoff accepted. Monitoring for 60 more minutes before closing.

Jamal Ortiz: marking this thread for postmortem and linking logs + Grafana dashboards. Case reference: AWS KMS 1234567890.

Alice Nguyen: thanks all. I'll update once rollout completes to 100% or if we see regression. :thumbsup:
